text:
carl: quick sync — proposing an 'elastic ramp controller' that emits short-lived allocation intents to reduce cold-start p95 for bursty tenants.

anika: high level?

carl: control-plane watches short-window qps spikes + p95 and emits signed intent: tenant, gpu_slices, duration_s, ramp_curve, priority_weight. operator can ack/partial/reject.

kevin: how is this different from prewarm tokens?

carl: prewarm is static. elastic ramp is telemetry-driven and time-boxed with a gpu_seconds budget per tenant to limit wasted allocations.

priya: operator must be able to decline. define lifecycle states: PENDING -> ACK -> APPLIED/REDUCED/REJECTED with reason. control-plane should fallback on reduced allocation.

kevin: packing hints? we need kernel_tags and elastic=true so operator can bin-pack safely. and a cooldown per-tenant to avoid oscillation.

anika: rollout: implement intent proto + verify JWTs, operator status path, simulate mode (would_apply), canary on dev pools, opt-in tenants for dedicated pools.

carl: metrics to add: intent_accept_rate, intent_reject_reasons, post_intent_p95, intent_cost_gpu_seconds, cross_tenant_arbitration_failures.

priya: testing: loadgen with burst shapes, mixed-model packing to surface kernel incompat and eviction cases. also ensure intent auth validated.

ops-bot: note: deploy window 22:00 UTC — avoid canary during window :calendar:.

kevin: ok. ACTIONS: carl write RFC + configs, priya scope operator API, anika add dashboards, kevin design load tests.

anika: one more — default off for enterprise; opt-in for hosted.
